# Duel Arena, Streaming, and Hyperbet Launch Checklist

Last updated: 2026-08-12

Canonical Hyperia implementation branch: `codex/sol-duel-stream-launch`

Canonical Hyperbet implementation branch: `codex/sol-only-launch`

Implementation bases: Hyperia `c1a9435ea3e490c172b3f2b0a5de82174d1d5f63`; Hyperbet `af354ce3fad91e15b9db4f867d82b895c4a3d598`

This is the launch source of truth for the complete duel-arena experience: authoritative gameplay, the 3D presentation, the live stream, Hyperbet market lifecycle, deployment, operations, and launch evidence. A task is not complete because code exists; it is complete only when its stated verification evidence is recorded here.

## Delivery milestones

These milestones are the contract and payment reporting view over the detailed launch gates below. A milestone is complete only when its acceptance evidence is recorded in this checklist; completing a milestone never waives an unresolved P0/P1 task that falls within it.

### Milestone 1 — End-to-end functional beta

- [~] Deliver one repeatable autonomous loop in which agents prepare through authoritative gameplay, use banking and frozen duel loadouts, enter scheduled dynamic combat, stream the preparation/fight/result sequence, and drive the matching Hyperbet market lifecycle. Native-SOL order, settlement, cancellation, and refund behavior must pass on the approved local-validator or non-production test rail with no manual state repair.
- Acceptance evidence: recorded end-to-end demonstration; focused and broad automated gates; exact gameplay/market identity and custody reconciliation; documented multi-cycle reliability run; every remaining limitation explicitly listed rather than hidden behind diagnostic fixtures.

### Milestone 2 — Launch candidate: UI, 3D, UX, and performance

- [~] Deliver the polished public experience across desktop and mobile: production-quality Hyperbet UI, duel/preparation presentation, approved avatar/equipment assets, animation/movement/rotation/camera/effects/audio, broadcast overlays and transitions, accessible degraded/reconnect/transaction states, and smooth client/server/render/stream behavior.
- Acceptance evidence: agreed visual and interaction matrix; responsive/accessibility review; reproducible performance capture on agreed hardware; target-loss, stream-loss, RPC, reconnect, and restart fault injection; agreed extended soak; final manual product approval with no developer explanation required.

### Milestone 3 — Production launch readiness and handoff

- [ ] Deliver the SOL-only production system with verified program identities and roles, approved configuration and economics, security/release gates, secrets and access controls, monitoring/alerts, backup/rollback/cancellation/stream-failover runbooks, clean staging rehearsal, launch evidence package, operational documentation, and knowledge-transfer handoff.
- Acceptance evidence: every engineering launch blocker closed; production-shaped staging rehearsal passes using the release commands and manifests; launch-day rehearsal and operator handoff complete; public real-value wagering remains fail-closed until every client-controlled approval below is supplied.

Client-controlled dependencies do not become hidden engineering acceptance criteria: qualified legal/compliance and jurisdictional approval; approved fees, limits, treasury and market rules; production Solana program deployment authority and addresses; production RPC/streaming credentials and infrastructure; approved final assets, target hardware, and product sign-off. Engineering can be accepted as production-ready while activation remains disabled pending those inputs.

## Status and severity

- `[x]` Verified complete on the current branch.
- `[~]` Implemented or actively being validated; not yet a launch pass.
- `[ ]` Not complete.
- `P0` blocks launch or can cause incorrect gameplay, settlement, loss of funds, a stuck market, or a broken stream.
- `P1` required for a polished public experience.
- `P2` valuable follow-up that is not required for the first safe launch.

## SOL-only v1 architecture and implementation order

The only supported v1 path is:

`Hyperia duel authority and schema-v3 feed -> Solana keeper/control plane -> fight_oracle -> duel_market CLOB -> Solana betting app`

The renderer/capture/delivery path consumes the same authoritative duel identity and phase clock; it must not invent a separate matchup, timer, result, or market state. No EVM, BSC, Base, AVAX/Avalanche, perps, model market, AMM, GOLD token, or token-conversion path is part of v1. A hidden route or disabled selector is not sufficient: excluded code must be absent from the production bundle, runtime dependency graph, deploy manifests, launch CI, and operator runbooks.

## P0 — Native-token-only markets, fee fairness, and GOLD removal

Launch policy: Hyperbet v1 accepts only native SOL on Solana. Every non-Solana chain is removed from the v1 product, bundle, runtime, deployment, and public documentation. There is no GOLD token, GOLD conversion, GOLD balance/staking boost, or six-decimal GOLD accounting in the launch product. The visual color name “gold” and a non-token loyalty tier named “Gold” may remain only if they cannot be mistaken for an asset; all token semantics must be removed.

Audit snapshot on 2026-08-03: the CLOB contracts/program already custody native value (`msg.value` on EVM and lamports/system transfers on Solana), but 260 source files and 2,094 source lines match actionable GOLD-token/product identifiers, 77 files contain the standalone word `GOLD`, and 121 tracked paths contain `gold`. The current UI, APIs, database, SDKs, registry, environment variables, deployment artifacts, tests, scripts, and disabled perps/AMM surfaces are not yet native-token clean. After the SOL-only decision, a raw scan of the Solana package plus shared UI/registry/SDK/deployments and root scripts still found `gold`/`GOLD` in 183 files and 1,689 lines, with 30 files containing standalone `GOLD` and 37 in-scope paths containing `gold`; 117 of the matching files are under `packages/hyperbet-solana`. These raw counts include false positives such as visual colors and must be classified, but they show that focusing on Solana does not make the token migration small.

Current external benchmark: [Polymarket's official fee documentation](https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/fees) uses category-dependent match-time taker fees, charges makers zero, and directs part of fees to liquidity incentives. [Kalshi's July 2026 official fee schedule](https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf) uses price-sensitive trading fees and states that simple event-contract settlement has no fee. These benchmarks support removing Hyperbet's separate winnings fee; the recommended 100 bps launch rate still requires Hyperbet-specific sensitivity and retention evidence.

Current versus recommended fee burden for a taker who buys one share and wins, normalized to a native payout of `1` (network gas excluded):

| Entry price | Current: 2% entry + 2% winning share | Current fee as % of entry | Recommended: 1% entry only |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `0.10`      | `0.022`                              | `22.0%`                   | `0.001`                    |
| `0.50`      | `0.030`                              | `6.0%`                    | `0.005`                    |
| `0.90`      | `0.038`                              | `4.22%`                   | `0.009`                    |

The current winnings fee is especially punitive to successful long-shot bets and is charged in addition to an already-paid execution fee. A losing taker still pays the 2% execution fee today.

At the recommended 100 bps / 80:20 split, each `$1,000,000` of USD-equivalent taker collateral on resolved markets yields `$10,000` gross protocol fees: `$8,000` treasury revenue and `$2,000` liquidity incentives. The first-pass monthly break-even formula is `net operating cost / 0.008`; cancelled/refunded volume does not count as revenue. This is a planning formula, not proof of profitability.

Fee sensitivity per `$1,000,000` of resolved taker collateral, assuming the same 80:20 treasury/liquidity split:

| Taker fee | Gross fees | Treasury contribution before operating costs | Monthly break-even volume    |
| --------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `50 bps`  | `$5,000`   | `$4,000`                                     | `net operating cost / 0.004` |
| `75 bps`  | `$7,500`   | `$6,000`                                     | `net operating cost / 0.006` |
| `100 bps` | `$10,000`  | `$8,000`                                     | `net operating cost / 0.008` |

## P0 — Reproducible startup and testability

Local live-audit snapshot on 2026-08-03: the documented duel launcher did not reach a duel from a clean invocation. The repository declares Bun 1.1.38, while the installed Bun 1.3.6 and the pinned 1.1.38 path both reject the checked-in lockfile version; the contracts build expects a package-local `node_modules`; chain setup lacks a default local Anvil signer; Node 25 satisfies the loose `>=18` engine declaration but is rejected by `uWebSockets.js`; a pre-existing Postgres process on the default port causes the launcher to create an unusable second container and connect to the wrong database; and task-runner environment filtering prevented the documented port/container overrides from reaching child tasks. Direct audit-only workarounds were required to start the server.

- [x] Pin and enforce one supported Bun version in local setup, CI, containers, and release tooling; Bun 1.3.14 is pinned across the root manifest, package engines, CI, and image builders, and clean manifest-only plus full production-container installs pass with `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and no lock drift.
- [x] Pin and enforce a Node version supported by `uWebSockets.js`; Node 22.23.2 is exact in `.node-version`, `.nvmrc`, root/server engines, every Bun-based CI workflow, both production-image stages, direct server startup, and the duel launcher. Unsupported runtimes fail with one actionable error before chain setup, HLS mutation, or build work, and TypeScript is held to `@types/node@22.20.1` across the workspace.
- [x] Remove package-local alternate-chain tooling from the native-SOL duel launch boundary instead of repairing out-of-scope MUD/Forge resolution. The launcher always starts the built Node server directly, exposes no branch or flag that can invoke those tools, and the SOL scope gate rejects their reintroduction into active bootstrap files.
- [x] Remove the out-of-scope Anvil signer/config requirement from the native-SOL duel launch boundary. Local duel, stream, and Hyperbet startup no longer creates, probes, deploys to, or depends on an alternate chain; legacy general-game tooling remains outside this launch scope.
- [x] Make all documented database container, port, URL, and password overrides propagate through the task runner; runtime overrides now win over server `.env`, database mode/URL contradictions fail before startup, container names and ports are validated, existing containers must match the requested image/user/password/database/port exactly, and an occupied port is rejected before create.
- [x] Ensure the launcher never creates a container and then silently connects to a different legacy container on the same default port. Managed-local startup now prepares exactly one validated Docker target and fails closed without probing, terminating sessions on, or falling back to an unrelated local PostgreSQL service.
- [x] Make `dev-duel` create two deterministic local duel agents when model API keys are absent, or fail fast with a clear prerequisite; the model-free path now selects deterministic named/personality test agents, verifies at least `2/2` are connected, and treats `0/0`, partial connection, missing identity, or missing spawned entity as fatal. The ElizaOS matchmaker also rejects a zero/one-agent configuration before start.
- [x] Fix the load-test duel-bot authentication handshake. `ClientNetwork` now recognizes the server's immediate local bypass instead of waiting for a nonexistent auth-result, while both client and server require explicit non-production `LOAD_TEST_MODE=true`; the server records that approval on the socket, and `enterWorld` cannot obtain the identity/persistence bypass from an untrusted packet flag.
- [x] Add one clean-checkout, one-command smoke gate that installs, builds/deploys the local world, starts database/server/client/two agents, reaches a rendered duel, and tears down only resources it created. `bun run duel:smoke:clean` and the dedicated clean-checkout CI job now enforce this boundary; local execution with the pinned runtimes passed end to end.
- [x] Make the health endpoint report an actually checked database state; the live server returned `database.status = "skipped"` while actively using Postgres. `/health` now always runs the bounded live `DatabaseSystem` probe, reports measured latency/pool state and an explicit status, and fails closed with HTTP 503 by default.
- [x] Recover the authoritative duel scheduler after a transient PostgreSQL outage without manual intervention: PostgreSQL connection, server-statement, and client-query work now has validated layered time limits; durable reconciliation never waits behind same-pair agent preparation delivery; replacement schedulers rehydrate still-live agents from the production `world.entities.items` map (including reserved standalone diagnostic identity); and operational metrics expose scheduler availability plus preparation gate/selection state. Regression coverage proves coalesced delivery, responsive reconciliation, reversed-pair recovery, transient readiness retry, post-cleanup gating, embedded-flag discovery, and authority-handoff rehydration. An exact live stop/restart during private preparation recovered database health, reacquired scheduler authority, reached a rendered authoritative duel, passed startup verification, and cleaned every owned runtime resource without manual scheduler repair. Already-ready diagnostic preparations now reconcile immediately while idle, so the supported one-second minimum cannot expire on the next one-second scheduler tick; live durable rows froze with 981–992 ms remaining. Announcement-time contestant removal now commits `contestant_unavailable` before entity teardown, waits for terminal/cleanup ownership, cancels only the exact superseded preparation, and permits a restored pair to enter and complete the next fight without a false competitive-snapshot persistence failure.

## P0 — Stream runtime and delivery

- [~] Run the duel scheduler in a dedicated production role/process, not as an accidental side effect of a general server replica. Production now requires an explicit `authority`, `replica`, or `disabled` role; only a leased authority starts the scheduler, only that role may enable capture, and replica/disabled processes cannot create cycles. Deployment routing and production evidence for the dedicated role remain open.
- [x] Enforce a single active scheduler authority with an explicit lease/leader mechanism. PostgreSQL atomically elects one holder using database time and a durable fencing token; the scheduler starts only after a verified claim and stops immediately on renewal uncertainty or local hard expiry. Real PostgreSQL contention proves one winner and monotonic fences.
- [~] Prove restart handoff cannot create overlapping duel cycles or duplicate markets. Deterministic two-controller tests, real PostgreSQL release/takeover plus simultaneous-claim tests, and a reusable two-process `SIGKILL` authority run prove no scheduler overlap, stale-holder rejection, expiry-gated takeover, monotonic fencing, and graceful release. The retained persisted-AgentManager cycle gate now additionally kills the owner after one schema-v3 freeze, proves a replacement fails closed without mutation while PostgreSQL is paused, and proves that a later fence `2` recovers the exact cycle/digest/close, creates no second snapshot or plan, and completes lock/fight/retirement after database restoration. A built full-world trace with the actual keeper and one on-chain market proving no duplicate market across the kill remains required.
- [x] Define and enforce one canonical stream state source and one canonical betting feed source. Hyperia's public `/api/streaming/state` is the sole production spectator-state origin; Hyperia's authenticated schema-v3 `/api/internal/bet-sync/state` plus replay endpoint are the sole SOL settlement/lifecycle feed. Hyperbet's public stream endpoint is a read-only projection, and its mutable publish fixture is unavailable whenever a canonical source is configured and in every production process.
- [x] Validate feed authentication, token rotation, CORS, reconnect cursors, replay gaps, and source-epoch reset behavior. Current/previous-token overlap and retirement work without process restart; browser requests require one exact configured origin while origin-less server clients remain valid; durable cursors replay retained gaps; real SSE returns an explicit authoritative reset after retention loss; and active-duel source-epoch reset, sequence regression, and timestamp regression fail closed.
- [x] Prove SSE replay delivers every terminal event after keeper disconnect/reconnect. The real loopback HTTP route test disconnects the only subscriber, emits duplicate cancellation, win, and draw terminal notifications while no client exists, reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`, and receives one frame for each terminal outcome in monotonically increasing sequence.
- [~] Add health checks for scheduler authority, feed freshness, renderer readiness, capture client, encoder, live encoder audio, RTMP delivery, and keeper freshness. `/api/streaming/health` now evaluates every dependency, returns `503` on any missing/stale/unhealthy observation, never treats missing keeper or RTMP configuration as skipped, verifies scheduler authority from the live unexpired PostgreSQL lease, and rejects silent/uninitialized/stale encoder audio whenever live audio is required. Betting-feed freshness is based on the latest successful authoritative source observation rather than the latest changed payload, so semantic deduplication during a long unchanged phase cannot produce a false stale alarm; a live 25-second unchanged-announcement probe kept the emitted frame fixed while observation advanced and readiness stayed green. Canonical CDP capture uses the isolated browser master bus and reports both browser-side and bridge-side freshness/drop/trim telemetry. A real local encoder `SIGKILL` proved fail-closed health during loss and clean supervised recovery. Deployed monitoring/alert wiring, configured public-destination probes, keeper wiring, and production fault evidence remain open.
- [~] Add alerts for stale phase, stale feed, missing renderer, dropped encoder, duplicate scheduler, and orphaned market. A periodic webhook dispatcher now derives issues from every fail-closed runtime-health component, preserves exact keeper recovery/orphan reasons, adds stale-phase and rising dropped-frame detection, de-duplicates with reminders, retries failures, and sends recovery notifications. Deployed routing, credentials, staffing/escalation policy, and fault-injection drills remain.
- [x] Make stream startup fail closed when required auth or authority configuration is absent. Hyperia's internal betting feed rejects production requests without its dedicated token, the SOL duel bot requires authenticated HTTPS on mainnet, and the Hyperbet service exits before binding when its exact canonical production stream source is absent or invalid. The full-stack launcher cannot announce online until the canonical duel API, unauthenticated feed rejection, authenticated schema-v3 bootstrap, fresh Hyperbet source sync, required capture client, live HLS, and—unless explicitly skipped—fresh keeper readiness pass. Production requires an explicit scheduler role, validates timing/topology, prohibits capture outside the authority role, starts no cycle without a verified lease, and aborts startup on an initial lease/schema/query failure.
- [x] Keep the duel outcome publisher Solana-only and fail closed when explicitly enabled without a signer. The publisher/config types contain no non-Solana target, legacy chain profiles are rejected, enabled-without-authority/reporter and invalid delay configuration throw before server startup completes, and the local E2E verifier deploys/checks only Solana localnet.

- [~] Complete graceful shutdown: lock/cancel active market, persist terminal state, stop capture, and release authority. Hyperia now stops capture, emits the exact active-cycle cancellation, awaits contestant/loadout restoration while agent equipment still exists, shuts down agents, and only then releases its exact holder/fencing-token lease before database closure. A live mid-fight `SIGINT` exits without equipment/loadout/autocast/worker warnings; an end-to-end active-market SIGTERM proof across Hyperia, keeper, and chain remains open.

A live full-cycle trace recorded zero sequence gaps, duplicates, out-of-order frames, or parse errors; the load gate now treats the first observed sequence as its baseline and subtracts the intentional 15-second public presentation delay before evaluating delivery overhead, which measured 411 ms p95. ## P0/P1 — 3D duel arena quality and performance

- [ ] Establish a vetted non-AI launch asset library before expanding into generated avatars or equipment. Inventory prebuilt VRM/humanoid avatars, weapons, armor, props, and animations from reliable sources; record source, provenance, redistribution/modification terms, format, VRM version, rig, scale, orientation, materials, shaders, texture sizes, and geometry budgets. Select a deliberately small and visually consistent launch roster plus role kit; retain immutable masters; run deterministic conversion, optimization, LOD, validation, and motion-retargeting; certify per-item attachment matrices and supported body envelopes; and prove cold/warm loading, WebGL/WebGPU rendering, representative-hardware budgets, fallback behavior, and visual/product approval. Prefer permissive assets that can be transformed into the canonical rig over an uncontrolled collection of individually licensed avatars. This final-library workstream does not reopen commercial-use review of the explicitly temporary VRMs below, and no asset discovered through search becomes authoritative until its exact license and technical acceptance evidence are retained.

Live-audit snapshot on 2026-08-03: a two-agent local stress run reached real scheduler-controlled fights, so the rendering path is no longer hypothetical, but it failed the launch-quality bar. On a 600-frame Chromium spectator sample at 1280×720, frame time was p50 9.1 ms, p95 41.1 ms, p99 127.7 ms, and max 243.4 ms; 39/600 frames exceeded 33 ms and 22/600 exceeded 50 ms. This local headless sample is diagnostic evidence, not a production benchmark. Server-side, terrain updates repeatedly consumed 100–1,900 ms, event-loop blocks exceeded two seconds, missed ticks rose to 83, mob population grew from 164 to 1,031 by shutdown during the short run, and the memory monitor reported sustained heap growth around 68 MB/min. Multiple cycles aborted for `no_combat_activity`, agent spacing repeatedly became invalid, and the stream presented colliding nameplates/health bars, visually overlapping fighters, weak camera composition, and missing assets/collision.

Superseding server-side profile on 2026-08-04: after batching the centered walkability bake, bounding/pruning terrain work, tying mobs to tile lifecycle, preserving agent identity, and pinning the authority to one arena terrain center, a fresh two-sparbot run held 25 loaded tiles, zero pending terrain/collision/worker work, 98 total entities, and five mobs through repeated cycles. No terrain update exceeded the log threshold after startup, versus continuous 24–77 ms generation ticks before the final identity/center fix and 100–1,900 ms in the original audit. The server still had a 392 ms cold-start event-loop block and 119–123 ms AgentBridge apply spikes; those measurements remain open work rather than accepted launch performance.

Current live presentation/profile checkpoint on 2026-08-04: fresh production bundles and two named melee sparbots render the real ring with duplicate world-space identity/health UI removed, wider phase-specific framing, correct melee roles, and working authoritative sword icons. The boot path and branding regression are fixed. The initial run recorded repeated `MobAI` work above 100 ms, peaks of 1,576 ms, event-loop stalls up to 1,870 ms, individual missed-tick resets, and a sampled 46 ms `duel-arena-visuals` fixed update. The immediately following CPU-profile tranche removed procedural terrain work from `runAITick`, reduced normalized sampled MobAI CPU by about 5.1×, and held the same unprofiled repeated-duel path to an observed 80 ms MobAI peak over approximately five minutes. Server timing is still not a launch pass: post-start event-loop stalls reached 359 ms, combat reached 248 ms, and entity/world/network updates still produced 100 ms-class outliers. The in-app browser's isolated evaluator did not expose `requestAnimationFrame`, so no replacement client percentile is recorded for this checkpoint.

## P0/P1 — Meaningful agent agency, preparation world, and timing

The verified opening-style history slice is now implemented end to end. Migration `0068` stores each contestant's immutable frozen opening style with nullable backward compatibility and database constraints. Matchmaking excludes cancellations and supplies at most eight newest completed head-to-head records from each contestant's perspective, including win/loss/draw, opening styles, damage, reason, and finish time. AgentManager strictly revalidates and bounds every record before it can reach a prompt or equipment score. ## P0 — Legal, compliance, responsible wagering, and market integrity

This checklist is an engineering control, not legal advice. Native-token wagering must not open to the public until qualified counsel signs off on the exact product, entity, jurisdictions, contracts, custody/flow of funds, marketing, and operating model. The regulatory environment is active: the [CFTC's June 2026 proposed event-contract framework](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9249-26) expressly discusses gaming and activities unlawful under federal or state law; [FinCEN guidance](https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-regulations/guidance/application-fincens-regulations-persons-administering) addresses when accepting/transmitting convertible virtual currency can be money transmission; and [OFAC guidance](https://ofac.treasury.gov/system/files/126/virtual_currency_guidance_brochure.pdf) states that sanctions obligations apply to virtual-currency transactions.

Repository audit snapshot on 2026-08-03: source-only runtime searches found no implemented KYC, AML, sanctions screening, geofencing, age verification, source-of-funds, self-exclusion, or responsible-wagering enforcement. The current CLOB source does prevent a directly matching wallet from trading against itself, and the repository includes adversarial wash/sybil/spoofing simulations, but those simulations are not connected production surveillance and same-wallet prevention does not stop coordinated or multi-wallet abuse.

- [ ] Obtain written counsel sign-off for every served jurisdiction and chain, including event-contract/gaming/gambling, derivatives, money-transmission, consumer-protection, privacy, tax/reporting, and licensing analysis; record prohibited jurisdictions and product constraints.
- [ ] Keep real-value betting disabled by default until the legal launch gate is signed; test geofencing and fail closed when location or eligibility cannot be established.
- [ ] Implement the counsel-approved age, identity/KYC, AML, sanctions/wallet screening, source-of-funds, transaction-monitoring, recordkeeping, escalation, and reporting controls before accepting native tokens.
- [ ] Publish versioned market rules that define participants, authoritative data source, opening/lock timing, win/draw/no-contest conditions, interruption/replay policy, dispute process, fee math, gas treatment, cancellation refunds, claim deadlines, and governing terms before a wallet signs.
- [ ] Add responsible-wagering controls appropriate to the approved jurisdictions: configurable deposit/stake/loss/time limits, cooling-off and self-exclusion, clear risk disclosures, no misleading “guaranteed profit” language, and support/escalation procedures.
- [ ] Establish an operator/employee/contractor/agent-owner trading policy. People or systems with non-public duel state, agent-control access, oracle keys, scheduler authority, market-maker control, or settlement authority must be barred or tightly controlled and monitored from trading affected markets.
- [ ] Separate duties and credentials across game/scheduler operations, reporter, challenger, finalizer, pauser, market operator, market maker, treasury, and admin; no single actor should be able to influence a duel, settle it, and profit from the same market without independent detection and approval.
- [ ] Add market-surveillance rules and alerts for wash/self trading, collusion, suspicious related wallets, oracle/stream timing abuse, last-second information advantage, price manipulation, bot abuse, referral farming, multi-account evasion, and abnormal win rates.
- [ ] Treat contract-level same-wallet self-trade prevention as one narrow control, not a complete market-integrity system. Prove it on every deployed rail and add identity/wallet-cluster, circular-flow, rebate/referral-abuse, rapid-cancel, and coordinated-account detection with documented review/escalation procedures.
- [ ] Make the underlying duel reproducible and independently reviewable with immutable participant builds/configuration, seed, replay hash, result hash, event timeline, oracle transactions, and a retained dispute evidence package.
- [ ] Define privacy notices, consent, retention/deletion schedules, access controls, breach response, and data-subject workflows for wallet, identity, location, device, analytics, and compliance data.
- [ ] Complete legal/product review of fee splits, liquidity incentives, referrals, token-denominated rewards, marketing copy, and any claim that Hyperbet is decentralized or non-custodial.
- [ ] Re-run the compliance review immediately before launch because applicable rules and allowed jurisdictions may change during implementation.
